wiki.api.title: API
virtual.list.view.summary: Virtualized presentation of large item sets as a responsive grid or list.
virtual.list.view.section.when.title: When to use
virtual.list.view.section.when.body: Use `VirtualListView` when a collection contains hundreds or thousands of similar entries. The factory creates only visible items and a small overscan; ordinary forms are better built with `VBox` or `LinearBox`.
virtual.list.view.section.style.title: Layout and StylePack
virtual.list.view.section.style.body: The viewport respects `layoutStyle().padding()`, `rowGap()`, and `columnGap()`. The same parameters can be configured through `StyleKeys.VIRTUAL_LIST_*` in a `StylePack`.
virtual.list.view.example.grid.title: Responsive grid
virtual.list.view.item.factory.title: Item factory
virtual.list.view.item.factory.summary: Sets the factory that creates a UI widget for an item index.
virtual.list.view.item.factory.parameter: Function from item index to Widget; null restores the default Label factory.
layout.style.title: LayoutStyle
layout.style.summary: Fluent layout rules for sizing, spacing, flex/grid placement, positioning, and overflow.
layout.style.section.overview.title: Overview
layout.style.section.overview.body:
`LayoutStyle` describes how a parent measures and places a widget. Use it through `widget.layout(style -> ...)` instead of calculating screen coordinates manually. Values are requests resolved by the parent: flex/grid rules, min/max constraints, and available space can change the final bounds.

The API uses CSS-like names but implements the UniGUI layout model, not full CSS. `margin` is outside the widget; `padding` is inside the widget and reduces content space.
layout.style.section.size.title: Size and positioning
layout.style.section.size.body:
Use `width`, `height`, `size`, and `sizePercent` for `auto`, pixel, or percentage requests. `minWidth`/`minHeight` and `maxWidth`/`maxHeight` constrain the result.

`fixed(width, height)` also disables flex growth and shrink. `fill()` requests 100% on both axes, while `expand()` takes remaining space only on the flex main axis. `position(PositionType.ABSOLUTE)` removes the widget from normal flow; combine it with `left`, `top`, `right`, `bottom`, or `inset`.
layout.style.section.spacing.title: Spacing and overflow
layout.style.section.spacing.body:
`margin(...)` separates a widget from its siblings. `marginAutoHorizontal()` and `marginAutoVertical()` let the layout engine distribute free space.

`padding(...)` moves content inward without moving the widget itself. `overflowX(...)` and `overflowY(...)` control content outside the bounds; `ScrollView` is responsible for actual scrolling when an axis uses `AUTO`.
layout.style.section.flex.title: Flex layout
layout.style.section.flex.body:
Set the main axis with `flexDirection(FlexDirection.ROW|COLUMN)` and wrapping with `flexWrap(FlexWrap.NOWRAP|WRAP)`. `justifyContent` distributes children on the main axis; `alignItems` controls the cross axis.

`flex(grow, shrink, basis)` uses weights, not percentages. Helpers express common contracts: `flexNone()` keeps the configured/content size, `flexAuto()` allows growth and shrink from `auto`, `flexInitial()` allows shrink, and `expand()` consumes remaining main-axis space. `gap(row, column)` controls line and item spacing.
layout.style.section.grid.title: Grid and alignment
layout.style.section.grid.body:
Define tracks with `gridTemplateColumns(...)` and `gridTemplateRows(...)` using `GridTrack.px`, `percent`, `fr`, `auto`, or `minmax`. `gridAutoColumns` and `gridAutoRows` define tracks created beyond the explicit template.

Use `gridColumn(start, span)` and `gridRow(start, span)` for child placement; starts are 1-based and non-positive values request auto-placement. `gridAutoFlow` selects the search direction. `alignSelf`, `centerSelf`, and `zIndex` customize one child without changing the whole container.
layout.style.section.update.title: Batching and copies
layout.style.section.update.body:
`update(style -> ...)` groups several mutations and sends one change notification after the outermost update completes. This is useful when a widget owns a live style callback.

`copy()` creates an independent style without the original callback. `copyFrom(other)` copies all values into the current object and preserves its callback.

widget.base.title: WidgetBase
widget.base.summary: Shared widget foundation for layout, StylePack lookup, state, rendering, events, and animation.
widget.base.section.overview.title: Overview
widget.base.section.overview.body:
`WidgetBase` is the common implementation behind UniGUI widgets. It owns the parent/child relationship, layout bounds, desired size, invalidation flags, style lookup, input state, animation controller, and render lifecycle. Concrete widgets extend it and implement their own content measurement and rendering.

The class is abstract: use a concrete widget such as `Label`, `VBox`, or a custom subclass.
widget.base.section.style.title: Style and layout
widget.base.section.style.body:
Use `layout(style -> ...)` for geometry and `style(...)` for visual properties. `style(String)` accepts declarations such as `padding: 8px;` and treats a string without `:` or `;` as a StylePack id. `style(Consumer<MutableStyle>)` is the typed alternative.

`styleId(...)` selects a named StylePack entry, `styleClass(...)` manages selector classes, and `styleScope(true)` limits inherited local-style lookup at the widget boundary. `layoutStyle()` returns the live `LayoutStyle`; changing it invalidates layout and visual state.
widget.base.section.state.title: Visibility, focus, and interaction
widget.base.section.state.body:
`Visibility.VISIBLE` participates in layout, rendering, input, and focus. `HIDDEN` keeps its layout space but suppresses rendering and input. `COLLAPSED` removes the widget from layout.

`enabled(false)` exposes the disabled style state and blocks interaction. `focusable`, `focusScope`, and `focusOrder` control keyboard navigation. `mouseCursor` affects the cursor only while the widget is enabled and visible.
widget.base.section.animation.title: Transforms and animation
widget.base.section.animation.body:
Immediate transform setters such as `rotationDegrees`, `opacity`, and `transformPivot` update the visual state directly. `animate(...)`, `animateOpacity(...)`, `animatePosition(...)`, and `animateScale(...)` use `TransitionSpec` and invalidate the visual layer while running.

`layoutTransition(...)` enables FLIP movement animation for layout-driven x/y changes; it does not animate size. Storyboards and spring animations share the same animation controller and are advanced by the widget lifecycle.
widget.base.section.render.title: Rendering, invalidation, and events
widget.base.section.render.body:
Call `invalidate(InvalidationFlags.LAYOUT)` when a change affects measurement or placement, and `VISUAL` for a paint-only change. Invalidation propagates subtree state to ancestors.

A custom `renderer(...)` replaces the standard visual but does not remove framework child traversal. Retained render caching is intended for stable leaf widgets; `renderCachingEnabled(false)` is appropriate for dynamic visuals. Register input or custom events with `on(...)`; dispatch them with `emit(...)`.
widget.base.example.configure.title: Configure a widget
widget.base.example.configure.code:
Label greeting = new Label("Hello")
        .id("greeting")
        .styleId("card")
        .addStyleClass("interactive");

greeting.layout(style -> style
        .padding(12.0f)
        .width(240.0f)
        .flexNone());

layout.style.method.update.title: Batch updates
layout.style.method.update.summary: Applies several layout changes and notifies the owner once after the outer block finishes.
layout.style.method.update.markdown: Nested `update` calls are safe. The change callback runs only after the outermost block, and only if a property actually changed. A null consumer is ignored.
layout.style.method.update.parameter: Callback that mutates this style; null is a no-op.
layout.style.method.size.title: Set pixel size
layout.style.method.size.summary: Requests width and height in UI pixels. The legacy `LayoutConstraints.AUTO` value becomes `auto`.
layout.style.method.size.markdown: This is a size request, not a guaranteed final size. Flex, grid, min/max, and the parent can still change the result. It does not disable flex grow or shrink; use `fixed` for that.
layout.style.method.size.width: Width in UI pixels, or `LayoutConstraints.AUTO` for content-based sizing.
layout.style.method.size.height: Height in UI pixels, or `LayoutConstraints.AUTO` for content-based sizing.
layout.style.method.padding.title: Uniform padding
layout.style.method.padding.summary: Sets the same inner padding on all four sides, in UI pixels.
layout.style.method.padding.parameter: Padding applied to the left, top, right, and bottom edges.
layout.style.method.flex.title: Flex shorthand
layout.style.method.flex.summary: Sets grow weight, shrink weight, and the base size before free-space distribution.
layout.style.method.flex.markdown: Grow and shrink are weights, not percentages. `basis` is the starting main-axis size; `auto` uses the width or height request. The parent may still change the final size.
layout.style.method.flex.grow: Share of leftover main-axis space. `0` does not grow.
layout.style.method.flex.shrink: Share of the deficit when children do not fit. `0` does not shrink.
layout.style.method.flex.basis: Base main-axis size (`auto`, pixels, or percent). Null becomes `auto`.
layout.style.method.grid.columns.title: Grid columns
layout.style.method.grid.columns.summary: Sets the explicit column template. An empty or null list keeps automatic columns.
layout.style.method.grid.columns.markdow: Each `GridTrack` is one column: `px`, `percent`, `fr`, `auto`, or `minmax`. Tracks created beyond this template come from `gridAutoColumns`.
layout.style.method.grid.tracks: Column tracks in order. Null or an empty list clears the template.
layout.style.method.center.title: Center children
layout.style.method.center.summary: Centers the container's children on both the main and cross axes.
widget.base.method.style.title: Inline style
widget.base.method.style.summary: Applies inline declarations, or treats a bare token as a StylePack style id.
widget.base.method.style.markdown: A string without `:` or `;` is passed to `styleId`. Otherwise it is parsed as `property: value;` declarations and merged into the widget inline style. Parser diagnostics stay in `styleDiagnostics()`.
widget.base.method.style.parameter: Inline declarations, or a StylePack id when the string has no `:` or `;`.
widget.base.method.animate.title: Animate a property
widget.base.method.animate.summary: Transitions a built-in property to a target, or applies it immediately when duration is not positive.
widget.base.method.animate.markdown: A matching in-flight transition is retargeted instead of restarted. Rotation uses the shortest angle path. A null property is ignored; a null spec uses `TransitionSpec.DEFAULT`.
widget.base.method.animate.property: Built-in property such as opacity, position, scale, rotation, or pivot.
widget.base.method.animate.target: Target value. Opacity is clamped to 0..1; non-finite values are sanitized.
widget.base.method.animate.spec: Duration and easing. Null uses the default spec; non-positive duration snaps to the target.
widget.base.method.layout.title: Apply layout
widget.base.method.layout.summary: Updates the live `LayoutStyle` and batches the resulting layout invalidation.
widget.base.method.layout.parameter: Callback that mutates layout size, spacing, flex, grid, or position. Null is a no-op.
widget.base.method.visibility.title: Visibility
widget.base.method.visibility.summary: Sets whether the widget is shown, hidden in place, or removed from layout.
widget.base.method.visibility.markdown: `VISIBLE` participates in layout, rendering, input, and focus. `HIDDEN` keeps its layout space but skips rendering and input. `COLLAPSED` leaves the layout and invalidates both layout and visual state. Null becomes `VISIBLE`.
widget.base.method.renderer.title: Custom renderer
widget.base.method.renderer.summary: Replaces this widget's standard visual with one renderer instance.
widget.base.method.renderer.markdown: The renderer draws the widget background and content. Framework traversal still paints children. Null restores the standard visual. Style-declared renderers apply only when this slot is empty.
widget.base.method.renderer.parameter: Per-instance `WidgetRender`, or null for the standard visual.
widget.base.method.invalidate.title: Invalidate
widget.base.method.invalidate.summary: Marks layout or visual state dirty and bubbles the flags to ancestors.
widget.base.method.invalidate.markdown: Use `InvalidationFlags.LAYOUT` when measurement or placement changes, and `VISUAL` for a paint-only change. The call also dirties the retained render cache. `NONE` does nothing.
widget.base.method.invalidate.parameter: Bit flags from `InvalidationFlags`, usually `LAYOUT`, `VISUAL`, or both.
